name: Chadian Boule
description: Boule, a stiff millet or sorghum porridge, is Chad's most essential staple starch, traditionally torn by hand and dipped into stew - real millet flour isn't a distinct item here, so this leans on cornmeal for a similar stiff, dippable texture.
steps_detailed: Whisk the cornmeal into 1.25 cups boiling water.
Cook, stirring constantly, over medium-low heat 15-18 minutes until very thick and smooth.
steps: Whisk the cornmeal into 1.25 cups boiling water.
Cook, stirring constantly, over medium-low heat 15-18 minutes until very thick and smooth.

name: Chadian Daraba
description: Daraba, a rich okra and vegetable stew often with real ground peanuts, is a beloved Chadian dish, traditionally eaten alongside boule.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion 4-5 minutes.
Whisk in the peanut butter with a little water, add the tomatoes and okra.
Simmer 15-18 minutes until well combined and thickened.
steps: Cook the onion 4-5 minutes.
Whisk in the peanut butter with a little water, add the tomatoes and okra.
Simmer 15-18 minutes until well combined and thickened.

name: Chadian Grilled Meat (Kilishi-Adjacent)
description: Grilled, spiced meat, echoing Chad's shared Sahelian grilling and drying traditions with its regional neighbors, made here as fresh grilled beef rather than fully dried kilishi.

steps_detailed: Mix the ground peanuts with the chili powder.
Coat the beef in the mixture and grill, turning, 6-8 minutes, until charred.

name: Chadian Fish Stew
description: A tomato-based fish stew, reflecting Chad's fishing tradition along Lake Chad and the Chari River.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion 4-5 minutes, then add the tomatoes and simmer 8-10 minutes.
Add the fish and simmer 8-10 minutes until just cooked through.
